title: role="text" must not wrap links or buttons
summary: An element with role="text" contains a link or other focusable item. Remove the role or move the link out of it.
problem: An element has role="text", a value meant to make some screen readers read a run of text as one phrase. It also contains a focusable descendant, such as a link. The role hides what is inside from the accessibility tree in a way that conflicts with that link.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users, mainly on Safari with VoiceOver, may be unable to tell a link is inside the sentence, or hear it merged with the surrounding words.
steps: Find the element with role="text" in the scan result and the focusable item inside it.
Remove role="text" from the container. Plain paragraphs and spans with a link read correctly without it.
If you need role="text" for split text styling, apply it only to a span that holds text and no links, buttons or inputs.
Re-check with VoiceOver that the link is still announced as a link.
whyItMatters: This is a recommended practice rather than a WCAG failure. Links need to stay discoverable inside a sentence, and role="text" gets in the way of that.
howToCheck: Re-run the scan, then listen with VoiceOver on Safari. The link should be announced as a link when you reach it.
